definitions.type: integer subalgebra of the universal enveloping algebra of sl2(C)
definitions.definition: U_Z is the integer subalgebra of the universal enveloping algebra generated by all X_r and Y_r for integers r≥0; its action on V is the given enveloping-algebra action.

definitions.definition: R=Z_(p)={a/b∈Q:a,b∈Z and p does not divide b}. It is embedded in C through Q.
M_R=R⊗_Z M; tensors use the natural integer-module structures.

definitions.type: R-linear map from M_R to V
definitions.definition: μ:M_R→V is the multiplication map μ(r⊗m)=r m for r∈R,m∈M. Its image is the R-span of M inside V. Identification of M_R with that image is made only after proving injectivity.

definitions.type: family of complex linear endomorphisms of V indexed by I×I
definitions.definition: For i,j∈I, E_ij is the unique complex linear map sending e_j to e_i and every e_k with k∈I and k≠j to zero, using the previously proved basis (e_k) of V.

inputs.statement: p is a prime integer, K is a field of characteristic p, and λ is an integer with 0≤λ<p.

M⊆V is an arbitrary admissible lattice: it is a free abelian subgroup possessing an integer basis that is also a complex basis of V, and it is stable under U_Z. No equality with the minimal lattice is assumed.

n=λ+1>0, I has n elements, and (e_i)_{i∈I} is a complex basis of V. For all integers d≥0, hy^d v=(λ-2d)y^d v, and for d≥1, xy^d v=d(λ-d+1)y^(d-1)v. For all d>λ, y^d v=0. For i∈I: xe_0=0; xe_i=(λ-i+1)e_(i-1) if i≥1; ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) if i<λ and ye_λ=0; he_i=(λ-2i)e_i. For every integer r≥0 and i∈I, X_r e_i=binom(λ-i+r,r)e_(i-r) if r≤i and is zero if r>i; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤λ and is zero otherwise.

output.statement: μ is injective. Identifying M_R with μ(M_R)⊆V, M_R is free of rank n over R, its complex span is V, and every X_r,Y_r (r≥0) preserves it. For all i,j∈I the integer binom(λ,j) is a unit of R and E_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1) X_(λ-i) Y_λ X_λ Y_(λ-j). In particular every E_ij preserves M_R.

locals.declaration: Choose an integer basis m of M that is also a complex basis of V, as supplied by H005. By N001 it has n members.
Define Q=Y_λ X_λ (the projector denoted P in the supplied proof).

argument.text: Choose the basis m from H005. It has n members because it and the N001 basis are both complex bases of V. The tensors of its members with 1 give an R-basis of R⊗_Z M: the integer coordinate maps extend to inverse R-coordinate maps, exhibiting the isomorphism with R^n. Under μ a tensor has these same coordinates as a complex linear combination of the members of m, so complex independence makes μ injective. Its image contains M and therefore spans V over C. Admissibility in H005 gives X_r M,Y_r M⊆M for every r≥0. Extending each operator R-linearly preserves M_R and commutes with μ. From now on identify M_R with its image.

produces.statement: μ is injective; M_R is thereby an R-submodule of V, free of rank n, spanning V over C, and preserved by X_r,Y_r for all r≥0.

argument.text: Define Q=Y_λ X_λ. On the basis N001, X_λ kills every e_k except e_λ and sends e_λ to e_0 with coefficient binom(λ,λ)=1; Y_λ e_0=e_λ. Hence Q=E_(λλ), and X_(λ-i)Q=E_(iλ), again with coefficient binom(λ-i,λ-i)=1. argument.text: For arbitrary i,j∈I, F002 gives binom(λ,j)^(-1)X_(λ-i)QY_(λ-j)=E_(iλ)E_(λj)=E_ij, as can also be checked on every basis vector. Substituting Q=Y_λ X_λ yields the asserted identity.
